methodTitle: A whole kit is not a checklist for everyone
method: Powerful fins can be heavy. An instructor’s favourite mask may not fit you. A continuous-harness wing can be a recreational choice when it suits your diving. Those conditions matter more than the length of a shopping list.

hollis-m1.purpose: A mask chosen for the face, not a best-seller list.
advantages: M1 is Vitaliy’s confirmed mask model. An uninterrupted view and a simple construction make it a useful starting point when finding your own fit.
limitations: Fit comes before brand. Check the seal, nose access and comfort with your hood. An instructor’s personal choice cannot guarantee a seal on a different face.
hollis-m1.experience: Vitaliy uses the Hollis M1. The current retail version has not been matched to his own example.
hollis-m1.accessoryTitle: Separate accessory: a neoprene replacement strap
hollis-m1.accessory: Hollis M1/M23/M4 Neoprene Strap replaces the silicone strap; it is not a sleeve over it. Check attachment and adjustment. Vitaliy used a soft headpiece on his spare Oceanic, but its brand and exact type are unknown.
hollis-m1.story: At Shark Point, Bonaire, a diver lost her mask. Vitaliy fitted his spare Oceanic to her underwater. Its soft headpiece helped avoid catching her hair. A spare mask can stay unused for years, then matter on one dive.

hollis-f1.purpose: When propulsion matters more to you than extra baggage weight.
facts: Standard F1 · not F1 LT or F2
advantages: Vitaliy deliberately flew with standard F1 fins. In his experience, their propulsion justified carrying the extra weight.
limitations: These are not lightweight travel fins. Their weight and negative buoyancy can affect leg position. Try them with your own boots and assess the whole configuration in water.
hollis-f1.experience: The F1 model is confirmed by the author. A current retail version or size is not presented as his personal pair.

hollis-st-travel.purpose: A compact single-cylinder wing without unnecessary harness clutter.
advantages: ST Travel follows Vitaliy’s criteria: one cylinder, a continuous harness and an aluminium plate for trips. For local dives he chooses steel as part of the overall weighting configuration.
limitations: 10 kg of lift is not a universal reserve for every cylinder, suit and ballast load. Balance and releasable weight require individual assessment; a continuous harness needs fitting.
hollis-st-travel.experience: The criteria are confirmed. Personal use of this ST22 / current ST Travel is not. This is a recreational configuration, not a claim of technical diving.

hollis-smb-spool.purpose: Make your position visible to the surface team.
facts: Finger Spool: 100 ft line · double-ended clip
advantages: Vitaliy uses a Hollis buoy and finger spool. The spool manages line while the buoy marks position. These are current candidates for that pairing, not a packaged shop kit.
limitations: Choose buoy size and line length for the conditions. Deployment needs practice; do not attach the line to yourself. A buoy cannot guarantee that every vessel will see you.
hollis-smb-spool.experience: His use is confirmed at brand level. The exact buoy and spool models in his own kit remain unknown.

scubapro-g2.purpose: A readable display and controls understood before the dive.
advantages: G2 is a currently catalogued Galileo option with configurable displays. Reading it on your wrist is a more useful selection test than counting modes.
limitations: Vitaliy’s own computer is a Galileo Sol, not G2. Check transmitter and package contents separately. Diveinn displays Notify me; stock of a specific configuration is not confirmed.
scubapro-g2.experience: Vitaliy uses his Sol with an independent mechanical SPG. The SPG backs up pressure readings, not depth, time or decompression calculations.

scubapro-go-sport.purpose: Colourful travel fins that fit the boots you actually dive in.
facts: Monprene · pink, turquoise and blue options
advantages: GO Sport offers a travel-oriented alternative to heavy rubber fins. The strap helps with donning; matching a mask colour need not change the fit requirement.
limitations: Do not confuse them with bare-fit GO Travel fins. Try the actual boot/fin combination. Weight varies by size; check the airline’s cabin baggage rules separately.
scubapro-go-sport.experience: Preliminary professional selection. Personal testing of this model by Vitaliy is not confirmed.

scubapro-trinidad3.purpose: A light, colourful mask — provided it seals on your face.
advantages: A coloured mask can bring the look of a kit together. Trinidad 3 has a simple frameless design, making it a travel candidate to try on first.
limitations: Colour cannot fix a leak. Check the skirt and nose access. The manufacturer does not offer prescription lens compatibility; consider another solution if correction is needed.
scubapro-trinidad3.experience: Not presented as the author’s own mask. A current option for evaluating fit and travel packing.

scubapro-navigator.purpose: A travel BCD with back inflation and a deliberate colour accent.
advantages: Navigator Lite earns a place here through its foldable design and two expandable size ranges. The coloured air-cell cover is an aesthetic option, not a reason to accept a poor fit.
limitations: An authorised technician must replace the coloured cover. Check fit with a cylinder, valve access, ballast and actual package contents. Diveinn stock of the required colour/size is not confirmed.
scubapro-navigator.experience: Current candidate selected against professional criteria. Vitaliy’s personal use is not confirmed.
